statement: After the conquest Hawazin and Thaqif gathered to attack first.

Anas: Hawazin, Ghatafan and others came with their animals and families; the Prophet had ten thousand and the Tulaqa'; the people fled; he called the Ansar to his right and left and they answered 'Labbayk, be glad, we are with you'; the enemy was then defeated.
The army entered the valley before dawn and Hawazin's archers were positioned on the slopes.

Al-Bara: asked whether they fled at Hunayn, he testified that the Prophet did not flee; Hawazin were archers and shot at them; Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith held the bridle of his white mule as he said 'I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked. Also used in chapter 2.

statement: Abdullah ibn Zayd: he gave the spoils of Hunayn to those whose hearts were to be reconciled and nothing to the Ansar; they were grieved; he addressed them ('did I not find you astray...'), they answered 'Allah and His Messenger are more generous'; 'are you not content that people go with sheep and camels and you go with the Prophet'; 'were it not for the Hijrah I would be one of the Ansar'; the valley of the Ansar; 'the Ansar are the inner garment and the people the outer'.
notes: Direct speech. Machine-checked for the first half; the second half from memory of the same narration. That it was the Qurayshi leaders who received the gifts is in Bukhari 4331-4337.

statement: He did not settle in Makkah but returned to Madinah.
notes: Undisputed; after the siege of Ta'if and an umrah from al-Ji'ranah. The siege of Ta'if is not narrated in this chapter.

statement: A Muslim delegation of Hawazin asked for their families and property; he said the truest speech was dearest to him and told them to choose one; they chose their families; he asked the Muslims to give up their shares willingly and they did; the captives were returned.
notes: Direct speech. Number from memory (al-Miswar and Marwan); not machine-checked.
